prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Several prominent open-source projects, most notably **curl** and **Python**, have publicly documented the burden of AI-generated "slop" in bug reports and vulnerability submissions. The maintainers describe this phenomenon as a form of denial-of-service (DDoS) attack on their limited volunteer resources, leading to burnout and, in curl's case, the termination of their bug bounty program.

Below are the documented examples and quotes from the provided search results.

### Curl (Daniel Stenberg)
Daniel Stenberg, the founder and lead developer of curl, has been vocal about the impact of low-quality, AI-generated vulnerability reports. In mid-2025, he described the situation as tantamount to a DDoS attack, and by early 2026, the project scrapped its bug bounty program to protect the mental health of its maintainers.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg characterized the volume of invalid AI-generated bug reports as a DDoS attack on the curl project's maintenance resources.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop," Stenberg added. | CLAIM: Curl implemented an immediate ban policy for submitters identified as sending low-quality AI-generated reports.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: Stenberg highlighted the significant emotional and psychological toll that processing low-quality AI reports places on volunteer maintainers.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We need to make moves to ensure our survival and intact mental health." | CLAIM: The curl project terminated its vulnerability reward program in early 2026 specifically to preserve the mental well-being and sustainability of its small team.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We will ban you and ridicule you in public if you waste our time on crap reports." | CLAIM: Stenberg issued a public warning that maintainers would actively ban and publicly ridicule users who submitted low-effort AI-generated reports.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly. They don’t really understand it, they haven’t really verified it." | CLAIM: Stenberg defined "AI slop" as reports generated without understanding or verification, characterizing the practice as a form of abuse against maintainers.

### Python (Seth Larson)
Seth Larson, a maintainer for the Python project, raised concerns in late 2024 regarding the cost and stress associated with investigating AI-generated security reports that appear legitimate but are ultimately bogus.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports." | CLAIM: Seth Larson noted that processing wasted time from low-quality reports leads to negative emotional outcomes including stress, frustration, and isolation for open-source contributors.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson warned that the burden of filtering AI slop contributes directly to the burnout of trusted open-source maintainers.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious." | CLAIM: Larson suggested that even if unintentional, the outcome of AI-generated reports is harmful enough to warrant treatment similar to malicious attacks.
